findings.result: Variant-from-type and type-from-Variant use placement copy construction into caller-provided storage; raw source wrappers construct once and destroy once.

Default constructor index0 constructs Vector<T>(); resize is a checked Error encoded through int64. Mutable index pointers address ptrw storage after successful resize; copied output Variant retains packed/COW ownership before local raw destruction.
Type conversion constructs retained Vector<T> copies. Read-only pointers live through synchronous collection; matching destructors release only those temporary copies.
Single precision Vector3 is three real_t floats/12 bytes, aligned4; std::array<float,3> provides the same12 byte capacity/alignment. No size overrun is identified.
Var has explicit Variant-copy construction; present uses are construction/return, not raw-array copy assignment. Non-elided return copies retain engine ownership.

ClassDB.class_call_static dispatches MethodBind::call; its ret is fresh NIL. Copy publication retains Dictionary/packed values independently of local out destruction. No pre-existing owned return resource is overwritten on this inspected path.
MethodBind update copies PropertyInfo/argument metadata, so temporary Name/hint buffers are not retained by address.
